column1: # Santali (Ol Chiki) word gold set, written 2026-11-18 from the descriptions below before the Santali rules
# were run on these items. Format: word, broad pronunciation(s) separated by |, category, source. Sources:
# U = word of the Ol Chiki descriptions: Everson, "Final proposal to encode the Ol Chiki script in the UCS"
# (Unicode L2/05-243R, 2005), the Wikipedia articles "Ol Chiki script" and "Santali language" (CC BY-SA 4.0),
# including the Ol Chiki text of the first article of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights quoted there;
# N = Santali numeral as listed in the Wikipedia article "Santali language" (CC BY-SA 4.0); C = word of the
# Santali locale of Unicode CLDR (common/main/sat.xml, Unicode License v3: weekdays, months, names of
# languages); I = word attested in Santali text of AI4Bharat IndicCorp v2 (CC0). Pronunciations hand-written
# with the letter values of Everson (2005) and Zide (1996) and the phonemes of Ghosh (2008, "Santali", in
# Anderson ed., The Munda Languages): ᱚ ᱟ ᱤ ᱩ ᱮ ᱳ = ɔ a i u e o, ᱟᱹ = ə, ᱮᱹ = ɛ, ᱚᱹ = ɔ; ᱸ = nasal vowel, ᱺ after ᱟ
# = ə̃; ᱻ = long vowel; ᱛ ᱜ ᱝ ᱞ ᱠ ᱡ ᱢ ᱣ ᱥ ᱦ ᱧ ᱨ ᱪ ᱫ ᱬ ᱭ ᱯ ᱰ ᱱ ᱲ ᱴ ᱵ ᱶ = t ɡ ŋ l k ɟ m w s h ɲ r c d ɳ j p
# ɖ n ɽ ʈ b w̃; ᱷ after a consonant = aspiration (kʰ, ɡʱ); the glottal letters ᱜ ᱡ ᱫ ᱵ are the checked
# stops k̚ʔ c̚ʔ t̚ʔ p̚ʔ at the end of a word, before a voiceless consonant and before ᱼ (phaarkaa), voiced
# stops elsewhere and before ᱽ (ahad); ᱭ ᱣ ᱶ after a vowel and before a consonant or the end of a word = i u
# ũ. Where a loanword is not said as its spelling would be read by these values (ᱟᱹᱵᱠᱷᱟᱡᱤᱭᱟᱹᱱ, b before
# kʰ), the expected form is the loanword's sound. Stress is not part of the expected forms (the evaluation
# removes it). Vowel quality that the spelling does not show (Wikipedia's transcription of the numerals has
# ɛ for ᱮ: pɛ, arɛ, ɡɛl) is not expected either: these forms follow the letters.
# Santali (Ol Chiki) sentence gold set, written 2026-11-18 before the Santali rules were run on these items. The
# first two sentences are the first article of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in Ol Chiki as quoted in
# the Wikipedia article "Santali language" (CC BY-SA 4.0); the others are lines of AI4Bharat IndicCorp v2 Santali
# text (CC0) that are in none of tools/eval/data/sat_dev.tsv, sat_heldout.tsv, sat_flores.tsv, sat_tatoeba.tsv and
# sat_wiki.tsv. Two of them (ᱟ.ᱛᱩ, ᱞᱟ.ᱜᱤᱱ) write ᱹ with a full stop, as some Ol Chiki text does. Pronunciation
# hand-written with the conventions of words.src. Format: sentence <TAB> pronunciation.
# Columns: id, kind, text, expected, category, source (with licence), split, date written.
